corrections.cooperating_attempts_serialize: `bootstrap.serialized` holds an exclusive flock on `<destination>/.bootstrap.lock` across custody, copy and publication, waiting up to `wait` seconds and then refusing by name. The lock is an owned path, so a link left at it is refused by custody, and it is opened O_NOFOLLOW because opening through a link somebody else controls would write into whatever it names.
corrections.custody_is_its_own_rule_and_is_asked_TWI: the owned-path preflight is `bootstrap.custody(places, destination)`, called by `admit` before any effect and again by `install` holding the destination's lock, immediately before the copy. What this attempt's own `prepare` legitimately made -- the stores, logs, state root, configuration and record -- is permitted; the runtime and the selector are not, which is what 'prepared once' means.
corrections.only_this_attempt_s_own_copy_is_unwound: a refusal after the copy removes the copied distro -- proved absent moments earlier under the same lock, so it is ours -- and touches nothing foreign, so a retry is not blocked by our own leftovers.
corrections.publication_refuses_rather_than_replaces: `instance.create` writes beside the name and LINKS it into place: one atomic operation that fails if the name exists. `os.replace` is atomic for a REPLACEMENT, which is exactly what must not happen to a selector that appeared while this one was being prepared. Whatever is there is left exactly as it was, bytes and links alike. `instance.publish` remains for rewriting an instance's OWN selector.
corrections.the_pinned_admission_is_still_pinned: the runtime manifest and identity carried from `admit` are what is compared and what is emitted; nothing re-admits changed bytes. The source-drift refusal still happens before the destination is created at all.

reversal_probes.method: each probe proves a PASSING BASELINE on pristine code, reverts one guard in an isolated COPY of the tree, and requires the named checks to fail ON THE INTENDED ASSERTION [J1]
reversal_probes.two_probes_first_PROVED_NOTHING_and_what: L2 (publication replaces whatever is there) and L5 (a refused attempt leaves its own copy behind) both passed against a selector that was already there before install -- because `custody` refuses that one first. The exclusive publication and the unwind own only the interval BETWEEN custody and publication, and I had written no test that reached it. The gap was real and is now covered by the injected-appearance test; the probes were re-pointed at it rather than counted. L1's intended assertion was also misnamed and corrected: reverted, install ACCEPTS the link, so the intended failure is the refusal that never came.

what_this_does_NOT_claim: these are deterministic filesystem interleavings, one of them injected at the step before publication. Nothing here is a concurrency test, and nothing here claims protection against arbitrary hostile mutation of the destination -- which is why the publication refuses exclusively rather than relying on having looked.
what_was_wrong: carrying the admission fixed one half and opened the other. An admission is a decision about a RUNTIME; it cannot promise the destination still looks the way it did while `prepare` composed an Authority into it. So `install(admitted=...)` believed a layout it had not looked at since -- and a selector that appeared meanwhile was OVERWRITTEN, and a state link that appeared meanwhile was accepted and a selector published that `instance.read` rejects on the very next read.
